key_insight: The paper estimates time-varying traffic flows from sparse aggregate counts by solving a weighted least-squares allocation over feasible region-to-region routes, without running a traffic simulation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a computationally light way to infer edge-level traffic patterns for smart mobility, urban planning, and sensor-limited transport monitoring.
method: Partition the city into spatial regions and generate feasible routes between them.
Build a weighted contribution matrix so sensors steer the flow estimate toward directly observable patterns.
Score candidate routes against regional count profiles to derive edge-level trajectories.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on the Brussels road network with real and synthetic data, reproducing daily traffic profiles and outperforming baseline methods at much lower computational cost.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on how well the feasible route set and sensor coverage represent the true network, so sparse or biased counts may limit identifiability.
paper_title: Simulation-Free Estimation of Traffic Flows from Sparse Count Data
